headline: Rate-hike fears turn the AI sell-off into a rout, and Asia's chip markets took the full hit

findings.headline: The AI sell-off is now a broad de-risking, not a sector rotation
findings.body: Anthropic's record listing did nothing to steady tech, AMD stayed under pressure after a short-seller report on its China links, and overnight the selling moved to the most chip-heavy markets in Asia, with Korea and Taiwan hit hardest. Foreign money leaving those markets alongside weak US breadth points to investors cutting risk across the board. The test today is whether Europe's chip names follow.

CNBC: AMD falls on short-seller report of alleged China exposure

findings.headline: Rates are the bigger driver: a December hike is in the price
findings.body: The Fed minutes and Governor Waller's talk of larger or faster hikes have put a December move in the price, which raises the cost of holding long-duration growth stocks. A firm dollar is draining non-yielding assets too, leaving gold on course for its worst week in eight months. Fed speakers later today and Monday's flash PMIs are the next chances to soften or confirm that pricing.

sources.label: CNBC: Strong dollar, tighter Fed bets leave gold at 14-month low
S&P Global: flash PMI release dates

findings.headline: A Danish link cut and weak wind keep southern Nordic power tight until 29 Nov
findings.body: TenneT has limited the DK1→DE link after urgent 400 kV disconnections, and the restriction runs until 29 Nov, cutting Denmark's interconnection with Germany while Denmark and SE4 trade close to German prices. Wind is running far below normal for the time of year, so the south stays expensive, while Forsmark 3 coming back has flooded the north. Until wind picks up, the north-south gap stays wide; hydro near normal means there is no wider deficit behind it.

view: Our view: this is no longer only an AI valuation story; a hawkish Fed is repricing growth stocks just as investors question how long data-centre spending keeps climbing. We would not buy the dip until Fed speakers or the flash PMIs soften the case for a December hike.
